body:
> Should all `SSL SYSCALL`s be considered for disconnect? 

It seems like that might be a good idea.  What research can we do on the nature of the "SSL SYSCALL" error, when such an error is encountered, does it always correspond to some corruption of the connection's state?   is there any chance that the current transaction is not lost?     are there docs for what this error is all about?

also note that at the moment, the "disconnect" condition results in *all* connections in the pool being expired since the primary thing we are worried about is the database was restarted.    is the SSL SYSCALL error infrequent enough that this is feasible ?

There's a tag on the error sometimes:

```
OperationalError: (psycopg2.OperationalError) SSL SYSCALL error: Bad address
FATAL:  no pg_hba.conf entry for host "10.244.65.66", user "app", database "benchling", SSL off
 (Background on this error at: http://sqlalche.me/e/e3q8)
```

> is there any chance that the current transaction is not lost?

Not sure. The error happens very early in the web request, in the first one or two db interactions (SELECT calls) of the web request, so there wouldn't be any data changes happening that early.

> is the SSL SYSCALL error infrequent enough that this is feasible?

We see it about once a week on one of our databases, so it seems reasonable. Do you know about how long it takes for connections to spin back up?

so by a "tag" you mean, if we read the textual string we can guess what it indicates?   

if the pool gets entirely invalidated, it's not that big a deal for it to spin up again.  it's just if some production app is getting random SSL SYSCALL errors on connections that ohterwise remain usable after the error is handled, this would make things worse.    I don't know the scope of what SSL SYSCALL errors cover, which is why I was asking.

> so by a "tag" you mean, if we read the textual string we can guess what it indicates?

Ah, my bad :) - by "tag" I meant that there's more to the error message text than I posted initially

Dug around some more, and found possible matches for the error messages:
https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/49223e106b0a43452d64b4e52719532012c81e25/src/interfaces/libpq/fe-secure-openssl.c#L214
https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/c9d29775195922136c09cc980bb1b7091bf3d859/src/interfaces/libpq/win32.c#L63

given that, I'm wondering if SSL SYSCALL means it's a networking problem, and it won't be possible to recover the connection.
it seems likely and we should probably just do it, I'm being overly cautious here

Jumping in and doing some sleuthing, it looks like any `SSL SYSCALL error: %s` from [Postgres](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/49223e106b0a43452d64b4e52719532012c81e25/src/interfaces/libpq/fe-secure-openssl.c#L214) is a `SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL` from [OpenSSL](https://www.openssl.org/docs/man1.1.0/man3/SSL_get_error.html), which is considered a "non-recoverable, fatal error".


>SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL
>Some non-recoverable, fatal I/O error occurred. The OpenSSL error queue may contain more information on the error. For socket I/O on Unix systems, consult errno for details. If this error occurs then no further I/O operations should be performed on the connection and SSL_shutdown() must not be called.

So with that in mind, it seems like all `SSL SYSCALL` errors wouldn't be non-recoverable. I'll work on submitting a PR unless you have any feedback.
OK it just means it will also invalidate the whole connection pool right now, which may be heavy handed.

issue.title: pool_pre_ping fails to reconnect on psycopg2 "SSL SYSCALL error: Success"
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

When a psycopg2 SSL connection to Postgres terminates abnormally, the error message returned by libpq will be sometimes be `SSL SYSCALL error: Success`.  This is a [known issue with OpenSSL 1](https://www.openssl.org/docs/man1.1.1/man3/SSL_get_error.html#BUGS), and anecdotally we still see it with recent versions of OpenSSL 3 on Linux when misbehaving network equipment causes the connection to terminate unexpectedly.  [According to the OpenSSL documentation](https://www.openssl.org/docs/man3.3/man3/SSL_get_error.html#SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL), any SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL is non-recoverable.

We are using `pool_pre_ping` to verify connections prior to check-out.  However, when a connection has failed with this error, no reconnect is attempted because this error is not [in the list of exceptions that are considered a "disconnect" event.](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/2607262110bdc5c5dc96fc19ddca895a15a58e4e/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/postgresql/psycopg2.py#L865).  We are attempting to use `pool_pre_ping` to work around an issue where a firewall between our service and the database will silently drop connections that have been idle for some time, so the desired behavior would be for it to re-connect when the ping fails, instead of throwing an exception.

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.0.25

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

psycopg2

### Database Vendor and Major Version

Postgres 13

### Python Version

3.12

### Operating system

Linux

### To Reproduce

```python
uri = "postgresql://..."
engine = sqlalchemy.engine.create_engine(uri, pool_pre_ping=True)
with engine.connect() as connection:
    connection.execute(...)

# Wait around for a while until misbehaving network equipment
# abnormally terminates the idle connection...

with engine.connect() as connection: # exception raised when pinging connection here
    ...
```
